text: In ethics, the distinction between a 'moral patient' and a 'moral agent' is best captured by which contrast?
choices: A moral patient acts rightly whereas a moral agent acts wrongly
A moral patient is always human whereas a moral agent is always non-human
A moral patient possesses rationality whereas a moral agent possesses only sentience
A moral patient is an entity that can be wronged or benefited (has moral status); a moral agent is one that can be held responsible for its actions
explanation: A moral patient is something toward which we have obligations because it can be harmed or benefited; a moral agent is something answerable for what it does. Infants and many animals are patients without being full agents. The other options confuse the distinction with right/wrong action, species, or invert the sentience/rationality mapping.
